newsitem.title: UK: Train firms plan new Oxford-Cambridge line-report.
newsitem.headline: Train firms plan new Oxford-Cambridge line-report.

text.p: Transport group Go-Ahead Group Plc could launch a new rail service between Oxford and Cambridge in southern England under plans for a new link being examined by local authorities, The Times reported on Monday.

It said that if the link goes ahead, it will be the first long-distance rail link to be built in Britain for 95 years and could also see services being offered by other rail operators including National Express Plc and Prism Rail, a train operating company.

The franchise to run the service is valued at 180 million stg, said the report, adding that talks are under way between the rail operators and the local authority consortium which is backed by Railtrack Plc, the rail infrastructure group which is responsible for tracks and signalling.
If approved, the service could take 2.12 million people off the roads each year. A transport consultancy has been employed to identify routes.
One possible route is a 100 million stg line which is seen attracting over 3,500 passengers a day and earning 13.7 million stg in revenue per annum.
The second possible route could cost 180 million stg, attracting 5,800 passengers a day and earning 21.1 million stg in annual revenues.
